title: Dynamics of Developmental Defect Formation
text:
Endpoint phenotypes resulting from genetic developmental disorders are well defined, but the molecular
mechanisms underlying the emergence of these phenotypes remain unclear. The proposed work will advance
the understanding of human developmental disorders by identifying the variability in developmental trajectories
that lead to a similar endpoint phenotype and the magnitude by which signaling needs to be changed to lead to
a qualitative phenotype.

title: Advanced Microscopy Core
text: PROJECT SUMMARY – ADVANCED MICROSCOPY CORE (AMC; CORE B) Core Leader: Dr. Michael Gerner The Advanced Microscopy Core (AMC) is an integral component of this Program Project Grant (P01), which aims to define conserved and tissue-specific mechanisms regulating Type 2 immune responses across the gut, skin, lung, and associated lymphoid organs. Many of the key processes under study—including neuro-immune crosstalk, dendritic cell migration and clustering, microenvironments involved in Th2 differentiation, B cell positioning, and tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS) formation—are inherently spatial and cannot be fully resolved using dissociation-based methods such as flow cytometry or single-cell RNA sequencing. The AMC will enable all participating projects to visualize, quantify, and compare these processes within intact tissues using cutting-edge imaging technologies and spatial analysis. Under the leadership of Dr. Michael Gerner, an expert in tissue immunology and spatial imaging, the AMC will provide centralized support for multiplexed confocal imaging, iterative IBEX-based high-plex microscopy, tissue clearing and volumetric imaging, real-time 2-photon intravital microscopy (2P-IVM), and advanced spatial analytics. The AMC will pursue three primary tasks: 1. Multiplexed Imaging of Tissue Microenvironments: Support high-resolution imaging (up to 15-plex routine, >45-plex with IBEX) in murine and human samples, and tissue clearing for large-volume imaging of intact organs. 2. Intravital Microscopy of Cellular Dynamics: Enable live imaging of immune cell behavior and interactions in skin, gut, lymph nodes, and lung explants using 2P-IVM and calcium reporters. 3. Quantitative Spatial Analysis and Mapping: Provide standardized pipelines for segmentation, phenotyping, cell-cell proximity analyses, microenvironment clustering, as well as cross-sample, cross- organ, and cross-species integration using CytoMAP and complementary tools. The AMC will provide uniform workflows, ensure data reproducibility, and foster synergy across projects through shared marker panels, centralized data infrastructure, and joint analysis meetings. It will also support cross- species comparative imaging to validate mechanistic findings from murine models in human tissues. By enabling deep, quantitative profiling of Type 2 immune microenvironments in situ, the AMC will be essential for uncovering how spatially organized cellular networks govern tissue-specific immune responses. The core will elevate the rigor, integration, synergy, and translational impact of the entire P01 program.

title: Programmable RNA engineering to target Integrator-mediated noncanonical RNA processing in neuroendocrine prostate cancer
text:
The development of targeted therapies for lethal neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC) remains an urgent
unmet need. This proposal aims to comprehensively define the novel regulatory functions of INTS7 in mRNA
3′end processing in NEPC, and to perform preclinical evaluations of nanoparticle-based CRISPR RNA
engineering systems for therapeutic applications. Successful completion of this project will substantially advance
our understanding of the Integrator complex in gene regulation and establish new paradigms for developing
therapies that target traditionally undruggable oncoproteins or 3′UTR alterations in cancer and other diseases.

title: Building Bridges to New Luciferins
text:
Fireflies emit light when an enzyme, firefly luciferase, oxidizes a small molecule in the
firefly called D-luciferin. Introduction of D-luciferin and this firefly enzyme into mice will
also cause mice to glow, and the bioluminescence produced can be used to report on
gene expression, enzyme activity, and the growth of cells in mice simply by taking a
picture with a sensitive camera. Our work seeks to modify these two components to
greatly improve the sensitivity and applicability of bioluminescence to image otherwise
invisible physiological responses in live animals.

title: PET Tracer for Imaging Cardiac Amyloidosis
text:
Cardiac involvement in amyloidosis (CA) is a major determinant of clinical expression of the
disease and may be present as transthyretin-related amyloidosis (ATTR) or mutated TTR
(ATTRv) or primary immunoglobulin light-chain–derived amyloidosis. CA shares several clinical
manifestations with heart failure patients with preserved ejection fraction thus the disease is often
unrecognized until later stages. Diagnosing cardiac amyloidosis in the later stages of the disease
results in poor prognosis. While the gold standard for diagnosing cardiac amyloidosis continues
to be a positive endomyocardial biopsy, it is an invasive technique thus prone to sampling error.
Other noninvasive morphological imaging techniques, such as echocardiography and cardiac
magnetic resonance have limitations and are less specific. Currently, cardiac scintigraphy using
99mTc-PYP (initially developed for bone imaging) scan is used for confirming presence of cardiac
ATTR is used as a standard of care in nuclear medicine. However, it lacks sensitivity to detect
prodromal stages of the disease, likely detects presence of microcalcifications within amyloid
fibrils, and lacks ability to quantify the misfolded protein. This clinical translational imaging project
is focused upon evaluating a new PET tracer, named herein as 18F-Fluselenamyl (18F-FSA) for
assessment of its sensitivity for differentiating ATTR and AL amyloidosis, while also ascertaining
its utility as companion diagnostic for stratification of therapeutic choices. 18F-FSA shows highly
promising data in 99mTc-PYP SPECT imaging confirmed ATTRwt participants on efficacy of
Tafamidis, the TTR inhibitor, while showing minimum effect on amyloidosis in ATTRv. These
preliminary data make it a highly worthy candidate for further exploration of its potential to acts as
a molecular PET imaging agent in ATTR and AL subjects with or without therapy. Overall,
successful realization of the proposed aims would facilitate translation of the candidate PET
molecular imaging tracer for noninvasive differentiation of ATTR and AL amyloidosis patients thus
transforming clinical cardiovascular healthcare space towards image-guided personalized
medicine for managing these patients.

title: Molecular and genomic basis of transposon-associated alternative splicing
text:
Transposons are mobile genetic elements that are normally suppressed in cells. When this
regulation fails, particularly due to dysregulated RNA-binding proteins and genomic mutations,
transposons can alter gene function through abnormal splicing. This project aims to uncover
how these disruptions occur across human tissues and diseases and to identify new strategies
to correct them, with the goal of improving human health.

title: Enhancing CAR-T solid tumor efficacy with secretory iRGD
text:
Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy currently has limited efficacy against solid cancers, largely
due to immunosuppression and impenetrability of the solid tumor microenvironment. Here, we engineer CAR-T
cells to secrete iRGD, a tumor-targeting peptide that increases permeability of tumor tissues and vasculature.
Our goal is to improve CAR-T cell infiltration into solid cancers and remodel the tumor microenvironment with
iRGD, leading to better therapeutic efficacy.

title: Non-canonical roles of Mitotic Arrest Deficient 1 (Mad1) in tumor promotion
text:
Cancer is the second most common cause of death in the USA. Mad1 (Mitotic arrest deficient 1) is
commonly upregulated in cancer, where it serves as a marker of poor prognosis. The experiments in this
proposal will define the role of Mad1 upregulation in tumor formation and metastasis, with the ultimate goal of
developing novel treatments to improve cancer patient outcomes.

title: Genomics approaches to investigate the evolution of germinal center responses
text:
This application is relevant to public health because it seeks to understand the pathways that regulate the for-
mation of germinal centers. Germinal centers are immune structures that are crucial to development of high
affinity and long-lived immune responses, which are necessary to prevent infections. Our application seeks to
understand the evolutionary underpinnings of germinal center formation in order to gain insights into the genes
and pathways that are needed for these crucial structures.

title: Strategies for targeting T follicular helper cells to improve HIV Env vaccine immunogenicity and efficacy
text:
This project will test strategies for targeting T follicular helper (Tfh) and cytotoxic (Tfc) cells to
improve immunogenicity and efficacy of mRNA LNP vaccines based on advanced HIV envelope
(Env) immunogens in nonhuman primates. Proposed vaccine strategies will directly physically
target Tfh/Tfc cells via surface-receptor engagement and also test mucosal boosting strategies
to generate an optimized HIV B cell vaccine

title: Structural Studies of Ion Channel Assembly and Signaling Complexes
text:
Voltage-gated ion channels (VGICs) are the targets of drugs used to treat hypertension, arrhythmia, pain,
epilepsy, and mood disorders. Our work aims to understand the molecular architecture that underlies VGIC
function and modulation and how such complex molecules are assembled. Such understanding has direct
relevance for development of more efficacious treatments of nervous system and cardiovascular disorders.

title: Machine learning approaches for the detection of emergency department patients with opioid misuse
text:
Opioid overdose is a leading cause of death in the United States with approximately 49,000 deaths and 1.5
million Emergency Department (ED) encounters related to opioid misuse annually. ED-based interventions for
opioid misuse are effective but limited in scale by barriers to the accurate detection of all patients who could
benefit from these interventions. This proposal seeks to use machine learning approaches to better identify and
characterize ED patients with opioid misuse so that timely treatments can be targeted to decrease opioid-related
mortality.

title: Artificial intelligence analysis of atrial remodeling evolution in patients with atrial fibrillation: Towards optimal ablation strategies
text:
RELEVANCE TO PUBLIC HEALTH
 The goal of the proposed research is to use a novel combination of imaging, artiﬁcial intelligence, elec-
troanatomical mapping, and mechanistic computational modeling to characterize atrial remodeling and under-
stand the causes for atrial ﬁbrillation recurrence in rhythm-controlled patients. Successful execution of the project
will pave the way for a paradigm shift in the clinical procedure of atrial ﬁbrillation ablation and in the quest to
eliminate repeat procedures, resulting in a dramatic improvement in the efﬁcacy of the therapy. The project will
culminate in a pilot prospective patient study that will test the new ablation strategy.

title: Lung Adenocarcinoma: From Genome Alterations to Therapeutic Discovery
text:
Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer death in the United States, with the major subtype being lung
adenocarcinoma. The goal of our proposed research is to use genomic approaches to understand lung
adenocarcinoma: how genome alterations in individual genes cause the disease, how we can find immunological
targets, and how we can understand genome-wide structural alterations. I anticipate that the insights that we
gain from this research could lead to new treatments for this deadly disease.

title: A cardiopulmonary unit-on-a-chip to investigate the pathophysiology and develop targeted treatments for right ventricular hypertrophy caused by pulmonary arterial hypertension
text:
Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a severe lung disease where narrowed arteries force the heart’s right
ventricle, responsible for pumping blood to the lungs, to work much harder. Over time, this extra exertion causes
the right ventricle to dangerously enlarge (maladaptive right ventricular hypertrophy, RVH), eventually weakening it
and leading to heart failure and death. While animal models are used to study PAH associated RVH, they do not
fully simulate human disease. We propose an innovative solution: a ‘cardiopulmonary-unit-on-a-chip’, a miniaturized
device containing human cells that mimics the key features of RVH and PAH. This chip has the potential to
revolutionize research by allowing us to study these processes in detail and develop life-saving treatments for PAH
and other heart-lung conditions.

title: AI-informed Signaling Factor Design for in vitro Rejuvenating Mesenchymal Stromal Cells
text:
Mesenchymal stromal cells are promising therapeutic cells that may treat many challenging diseases, yet very
difficult to produce as they often rapidly age and lose their therapeutic functions during expansion. This proposal
will develop an AI-based method for designing the drugs that can delay the MSC aging process by controlling
the biochemical signaling of the MSCs. Upon completion, this proposal will enable us to produce highly
therapeutic potent MSCs in a reproducible manner and advance fundamental understandings in aging signaling
of MSCs.

title: CRCNS: Waste-clearance flows in the brain measured using physics-informed neural network
text: Diseases like Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s are linked to buildup of waste in the brain. Much waste is cleared by the circulation of water-like fluids through the brain, but the pathways, velocities, and pressures of that circulation are not yet known. Measuring their details directly is not possible because optical methods produce only sparse measurements and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) cannot capture small structures or fast changes. This project will use artificial intelligence to augment optical and MRI measurements with the known laws of fluid dynamics, inferring accurate velocities and pressures with great detail. Major pathways will be revealed, and key information will be provided for modelers and clinicians investigating what drives the circulation. That knowledge could help detect Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s diseases before other symptoms arise and might enable doctors to prevent or cure them.

title: Microbiome-Mediated Tumor Immunomodulation in a Pathomimetic Colorectal Cancer Chip
text:
The vast majority of CRC patients with MMR-p and MSS tumors do not respond to ICI immunotherapy, with over
95% showing unresponsiveness. To tackle this challenge, we propose a patient-derived CRC Chip model
combined with quantitative molecular analyses to explore the microbiome's influence on ICI modulation in
unresponsive tumors. Through this approach, we aim to provide a mechanism-driven translational impact,
considering genetic, sociodemographic, and microbial factors, to enhance our understanding of
immunotherapeutic responsiveness.

title: Training in Tumor Virology
text:
Principal Investigator: Robertson, Erle S.
Narrative:
The Tumor Virology Training Program at the University of Pennsylvania serves as the central
forum for facilitating interactions among investigators involved in cancer-related viral research
on the Penn campus which provides a more directed training for trainees.

title: Deuterium metabolic imaging (DMI) of the heart: Application to Ischemia
text:
A new contrast agent for MRI uses “heavy hydrogen” tagged onto the body’s energy sources (glucose or fatty
acids), and then uses MRI imaging to identify where these energy sources travel and how they are
metabolized by the heart. We will image controls and patients with ischemia (low oxygen available for their
heart) and seek differences in energy utilization, to understand this type of heart-disease.
